title: Resting magnetoencephalography alterations in severe mental illnesses: A systematic review
title_zh: 重性精神疾病静息态磁脑图谱改变：系统综述
abstract: Schizophrenia, major depressive disorder (MDD), and bipolar disorder (Severe Mental Illnesses: SMIs), share genetic risk and brain structural changes, but their neural mechanisms remain unclear. Magnetoencephalography (MEG), with millisecond precision, enables direct examination of shared and disorder-specific disturbances in the timing of spontaneous brain activity. We reviewed resting-state MEG evidence on spectral power, connectivity, information-theoretic complexity, and brain dynamics across SMIs. A comprehensive search yielded 62 studies. Three reviewers screened, retrieved, and extracted data on MEG-related variables across regional activity (power), coordination of activity (connectivity, coherence, synchrony), regularity of activity (complexity, entropy), and overall dynamics. Three principal findings come forth. Beta oscillations emerge as a promising, albeit yet unconfirmed, candidate transdiagnostic signal, with increased power now reported across independent investigations of all three disorders and correlating with hallucinations, sleep disturbances, and cognitive deficits, consistent with disrupted predictive processing. However, direct within-study cross-diagnostic comparisons remain sparse (2 of 62 studies). Preliminary support exists for complexity-age dissociation to partition SMIs into neuroprogressive and state-dependent trajectories: neural complexity declines with age in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (opposite to healthy aging), while depression preserves the normative trajectory. Slow-wave activity diverges sharply: schizophrenia shows a widespread increased slow-wave dominance, while mood disorders show a decrease in activity. We propose a temporal disorganisation spectrum of SMI from excessive fragmentation (schizophrenia) to pathological rigidity (depression), with bipolar disorder occupying an intermediate position. This framework offers biomarker-type utility for stratifying illness severity, tracking neuroprogression, and identifying transdiagnostic therapeutic targets, particularly beta-modulatory neuromodulation interventions applicable across SMIs. Protocol registration: Open Science Framework (http://osf.io/v2gtb/).
abstract_zh: 精神分裂症、重性抑郁障碍（MDD）和双相障碍（SMI，严重精神疾病）共享遗传风险和脑结构改变，但其神经机制仍不清晰。磁脑图（MEG）具有毫秒级时间分辨率，可直接检验SMI中自发脑活动时序的共享与特异性紊乱。我们回顾了关于SMI静息态MEG的证据，包括频谱功率、功能连接、信息熵/复杂性与脑动力学。系统检索纳入62项研究。三位评审者筛选、检索并提取MEG相关变量，覆盖区域活动（功率）、活动协调（连接性、相干性、同步性）、活动规律性（复杂性、熵）及总体动力学。出现三条主要发现。第一，β振荡在跨诊断层面上是有前景但尚未确证的候选信号：在三种障碍的独立研究中均报告其功率升高，并与幻觉、睡眠障碍及认知缺陷相关，符合预测编码受损的图景。第二，现有研究中真正的同一研究内跨诊断比较仍然稀缺（62项中仅2项）。第三，复杂性-年龄解耦为SMI提供了初步支持，将其区分为神经进展型与状态依赖型轨迹：神经复杂性在精神分裂症与双相障碍中随年龄下降（与健康老化相反），而抑郁症维持了正常老化轨迹。慢波活动则分化明显：精神分裂症表现为广泛增强的慢波主导，而情绪障碍表现为活动降低。我们提出一种SMI时间失序谱，从过度碎片化（精神分裂症）到病理性僵硬化（抑郁症），双相障碍居中间位置。该框架具有生物标志物式效用，可用于分层疾病严重度、追踪神经进展，并识别跨诊断治疗靶点，尤其是可跨SMI应用的β调制神经调控干预。协议注册：Open Science Framework（http://osf.io/v2gtb/）。
